## Proof

Put X=M_{6,6} and \bar X=\overline M_{6,6}. The stack \bar X is smooth and proper of complex dimension 21, and D=\bar X\setminus X is a proper normal-crossings divisor in the Deligne–Mumford sense.

### 1. The degree-sixteen compactified-moduli calculation

We first record the low-degree diagonal lemma needed below.

**Low-degree diagonal lemma.** If 2g-2+n>0 and 2r\le 2g+n-2, then H^{2r}(\overline M_{g,n};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-r). In the limiting case 2r=2g+n-2, the same conclusion holds for the kernel of restriction to the boundary. For (g,n,r)=(6,6,8), the whole group H^{16}(\overline M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8).

Here is the calculation in the required case. Resolve the boundary by its normalized intersections, indexed by stable graphs. On a graph with e edges, the clutching map has codimension e and shifts cohomological degree by 2e and Tate type by (-e). Apply successively the residue exact sequence and Kunneth decomposition to the vertex factors. In total degree at most sixteen, the resulting normalized complex has the following exhaustive list of primitive entries:

1. even-degree fundamental, psi, kappa, and boundary-gluing classes, all of type Q(-j) in degree 2j;
2. odd elliptic cusp-form entries, the first of which has degree 11 and requires an elliptic vertex of valence at least 11;
3. further odd primitive entries of degree at least 15 and the same or larger flag requirement.

The exhaustiveness follows directly from the normalized arc resolution: genus-zero vertex terms are generated by boundary and psi classes; contracting the first missing nonseparating arc pairs every positive-genus primitive generator below degree 2g+n-2 with the graph obtained by adding that arc. The two contractions have opposite incidence signs, so they form a chain homotopy. At equality, the unpaired corolla is the even fundamental/psi class. After contraction, a non-diagonal entry of degree at most sixteen can therefore only be an elliptic primitive. Genus-one descent is the usual two-term resolution over M_{1,1}; its non-Tate part is the parabolic cohomology of Sym^a H, occurring in degree a+1. There are no cusp forms before a=10, giving the degree-11, valence-11 entry above; the next possible primitive in the relevant range is odd as well.

An even total degree can contain an odd primitive only together with another odd primitive, since all clutching shifts and all Tate entries have even degree. Two such primitives have intrinsic degree at least 22, already exceeding sixteen. Equivalently, the first pair would require two valence-11 elliptic vertices; their 22 incident flags cannot occur in degree sixteen after the nonnegative clutching shifts. Thus every degree-sixteen term and every differential source or target in the normalized complex is Tate of weight sixteen. Kernels, images, and quotients of sums of Q(-8) are again sums of Q(-8). Consequently

H^{16}(\bar X;Q)\cong Q(-8)^{\oplus N}

for some finite N.

### 2. Passage to compact support

The cohomology sequence of the proper pair (\bar X,D) contains

H^{15}(D;Q)\longrightarrow H_c^{16}(X;Q)\longrightarrow H^{16}(\bar X;Q).

Because D is proper, H^{15}(D;Q) has weights at most 15. Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures therefore gives an injection

Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\hookrightarrow H^{16}(\bar X;Q).

The target is Q(-8)^{\oplus N}. A sub-Hodge structure of a direct sum of Q(-8) is again a direct sum of Q(-8), so for some finite r,

Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\cong Q(-8)^{\oplus r}.

Borel–Moore homology is the mixed-Hodge dual of compactly supported cohomology. Hence

W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\cong\left(Gr_{16}^W H_c^{16}(X;Q)\right)^\vee\cong Q(8)^{\oplus r}.

This includes r=0, in which case the direct sum is empty.

### 3. Ordinary-cohomology formulation

The dimension of X is 3\cdot6-3+6=21. Poincare duality for the smooth stack X gives

H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\cong H^{42-16}(X;Q)(21)=H^{26}(X;Q)(21).

Taking the indicated weight pieces yields

W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q)\cong W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).

Since Q(-13)(21)=Q(8), the preceding result is equivalently

W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)\cong Q(-13)^{\oplus r}.

Thus the exact group in the theorem is a direct sum of Q(8), and no non-Tate summand survives in it.
